Cc: procurement@datascale.com

Subject: Clarify AWS private offer list price anchoring + reseller split

Hi Alex / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — product looked great. Procurement asked me to confirm a couple of items before we move to procurement review:

1) For the AWS Private Offer, can you confirm whether the public listing price in Marketplace will be used as the list-price anchor for reseller commission calculations, or whether Redwood will publish a separate list price for the private offer? We need this because our finance team nets downstream reseller pass-throughs against the public list price.

2) Our channel team usually requires a 12% pass-through to our reseller partner (CloudBridge). Can you confirm whether Redwood can structure the private offer such that the channel margin is passed through (no hidden holdbacks), and whether we need to document that in the SOW/PO?

3) Any evidence you can share on how previous customers treated list-price anchoring for private offers (short example or a stub) would help speed up our internal sign-off.

Attaching the draft SOW and estimated consumption worksheet.

Attachment: DataScale_PO_SOW.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Maya

Subject: Re: Clarify AWS private offer list price anchoring + reseller split

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) List-price anchoring: For AWS Private Offers we typically leave the public (marketplace) SKU list price as the canonical list price. The private offer applies a discounted price to that SKU for your account. If you need Redwood to publish a separate list price for accounting reasons we can do that as an exception, but there is an operational lead time and additional bookkeeping on our side.

2) Reseller pass-through: We can structure the private offer such that the discount applied is sufficient for you to pass-through 12% to CloudBridge without Redwood claiming a holdback, provided the pricing bands and SKU mapping align. The usual mechanism is: publish marketplace list price P, private offer net price N to DataScale, and document the reseller pass-through in the SOW so there’s a paper trail for audits.

3) Evidence: attaching a short channel margin workup we use internally (redacted). Also copying Kimberly from Partner Ops who will confirm exact language we can add to the terms.

Proposed immediate next step: Kimberly, can you prepare two short bullets we can insert into the PO/SOW: (a) statement that the private offer is applied to marketplace SKU listed price P, and (b) a one-line commitment that Redwood will not apply a separate internal holdback for pass-through to named reseller CloudBridge. If OK I’ll send a redlined terms doc back to Maya and procurement.

Attachment: channel_margin_workup.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Alex

Alex / Ben — please pick one of the two options below. I recommend Option B for audit clarity.

Option A (minimal): 
"The AWS Private Offer discount will be applied to the marketplace SKU list price. Redwood will invoice DataScale the agreed private-offer net price; DataScale may pass through up to 12% of the list price to its named reseller CloudBridge Partners."

Quick finance note — Option B is fine from a revenue recognition perspective as long as:

• The SOW or PO explicitly names CloudBridge Partners and the 12% pass-through is expressed as a commission percent of the marketplace list price;
• Invoicing: Redwood invoices DataScale for the private-offer net price N; any reseller commission is treated as a subcontractor/commission for DataScale, not a deduction on Redwood revenue;
• Taxes: DataScale must provide the reseller's tax ID for our records if CloudBridge will be receiving funds via pass-through.

I recommend the following exact sentence for insertion into the SOW (Laura suggestion):
"DataScale may pass through a 12% reseller commission to CloudBridge Partners measured against the marketplace SKU list price; Redwood will invoice DataScale for the private-offer net price and will not apply any additional holdbacks related to such pass-through, provided CloudBridge Partners is named in this SOW and DataScale furnishes the reseller's tax ID to Redwood's finance team prior to the first invoice."

If that language is acceptable I can sign off and Alex can issue the redline.

—Laura
